items.title: Why the Data Center Fight Has Little to Do With AI
items.summary: Texas hits pause, New York signs a moratorium, and 219 local bans pile up — but ten days of on-the-ground reporting from the Midwest suggests the data center revolt is less about AI itself than about NDAs, broken promises, and a world people feel is being imposed on them without consent. Plus: a White House safety-testing framework so secret even AI companies won't be told how it works, and SpaceX's first earnings as a public company.
items.whyItMatters: Infrastructure news is the supply side of AI: chips, memory, and hosting constraints quietly decide what tools can exist and what they cost.

brief.whatHappened: Why the Data Center Fight Has Little to Do With AI
brief.whoItAffects: Anyone affected by AI compute cost, speed, availability, or hardware supply.
brief.practicalImpact: Infrastructure shifts often show up later as cheaper tools, higher limits, or new bottlenecks.
